title: Identifying the characteristics of effective teacher professional development: a critical review
extended_summary:
This paper critically examines the evidence base behind the widely cited consensus that effective teacher professional development (PD) is sustained, collaborative, subject-specific, includes outside expertise, has teacher buy-in, and is practice-based. The authors argue that this consensus has influenced policy and practice in multiple countries, but that the reviews supporting it often rely on weak inclusion criteria and flawed inferential logic.

Rather than evaluating a single PD intervention, the paper is a methodological review of prior reviews and meta-reviews. It traces the literature from policy guidance back through umbrella reviews and then to the primary studies they relied on, focusing on studies that used pupil achievement as the outcome. The paper uses instructional coaching as an illustrative example of how to identify effective PD characteristics by combining causal evidence of impact with separate evidence on mechanisms such as habit formation and repeated practice.

The population of interest is K-12 teachers and their students, especially in elementary, middle, and high school settings, with much of the cited evidence centered on mathematics, literacy, and science PD. The authors conclude that many commonly asserted PD features lack strong evidential warrant, especially collaboration and buy-in, and that apparent regularities in effective interventions do not by themselves prove those features are causally important. They recommend a more theory-informed approach that links rigorous intervention evaluations with independent evidence about learning and behavior-change mechanisms.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring / adaptive instructional support system that provides guided practice, feedback, and/or individualized instructional assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Not the focus of this paper. The paper is a critical review of teacher professional development and does not evaluate a specific AI tool; it mentions instructional coaching and several non-AI PD studies as illustrative examples.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a critical review of teacher professional development, not an empirical study of an AI tool. It contains no direct evaluation of any generative AI system or other AI educational product.
impact_tier_rationale: No tool was evaluated, so there are no measurable effects on teacher practice or student outcomes to classify. The paper is theoretical/methodological rather than impact-evaluative.
